newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut may hold new tender for 35,000 T wheat soon.
newsitem.headline: Beirut may hold new tender for 35,000 T wheat soon.

text.p: Lebanon's economy ministry said on Tuesday it may hold new tenders for the purchase on its behalf of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat on international markets within the next two weeks.

"We may hold a new tender in the coming two weeks for the same quantity, 35,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat," an offical of the Office of Cereals and Sugar Beet told Reuters. The ministry on Tuesday rejected seven bids for the purchase of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat, dismissing the prices as unsuitable.
"We are not in need of buying wheat urgently at present. This quantity is for storage," the official said.
"We have about 35,000 tonnes of wheat in storage, and the private sector has 70,000 to 80,000 tonnes in addition to 30,000 tonnes arriving for two (Beirut) mills on March 1," the official added.

The cereals office is part of the economy ministry, which periodically invites international grain companies or their Beirut agents to tender to buy wheat on the international markets on behalf of the Lebanese government.
Local firms also make purchases for the private sector.
Lebanon has yearly wheat requirements of 400,000 tonnes.

The official said earlier seven local firms have submitted bids for the purchase of 35,000 tonnes of Hard Red Winter wheat on behalf of the ministry, with prices ranging from $203 to $207 per tonne, but all bids were turned down on Tuesday.

"Seven firms took part in the tender but all the bids were rejected. The prices were deemed by the minister to be unsuitable especially as Egypt bought wheat yesterday at $167 per tonne," the official said.

The economy ministry invited bids on February 7 saying the wheat was for March 15-31 shipment CIF to Beirut port silos. On January 8 the ministry said it planned to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later in the month but it never invited tenders.
